description: Regional spillover proxy coefficients for V3.1. Real bilateral spillovers deferred to V3.2.
methodology: Spillover strength based on regional economic integration levels (trade intensity, FDI flows, policy coordination). Regional leaders identified by GDP share and institutional influence.

east_asia_pacific.name: East Asia & Pacific
east_asia_pacific.rationale: High trade integration, supply chain dependencies, coordinated monetary policies

europe_central_asia.name: Europe & Central Asia
europe_central_asia.rationale: EU single market, Eurozone monetary union, high labor mobility

latin_america_caribbean.name: Latin America & Caribbean
latin_america_caribbean.rationale: Mercosur/Pacific Alliance integration, commodity price linkages

middle_east_north_africa.name: Middle East & North Africa
middle_east_north_africa.rationale: Oil price coordination (OPEC), GCC integration, labor migration

north_america.name: North America
north_america.rationale: USMCA deep integration, supply chains, financial market linkages

south_asia.name: South Asia
south_asia.rationale: Lower formal integration, but significant remittance and labor flows

sub_saharan_africa.name: Sub-Saharan Africa
sub_saharan_africa.rationale: Growing AfCFTA integration, but historically fragmented markets

western_europe.name: Western Europe
western_europe.rationale: EU/EEA deep integration, Eurozone, Schengen labor mobility

eastern_europe.name: Eastern Europe
eastern_europe.rationale: EU integration, German supply chain dependencies

central_asia.name: Central Asia
central_asia.rationale: Russia/China dual influence, commodity exports, remittances

southeast_asia.name: Southeast Asia
southeast_asia.rationale: ASEAN integration, manufacturing supply chains, China linkages

global_powers.description: Countries with global (not just regional) spillover effects

usage.example: If China GDP +2%, East Asia regional spillover = 2% * 0.45 = +0.9%
caveats: Proxy estimates only - real bilateral effects may differ
Does not capture bilateral heterogeneity (e.g., Vietnam vs Japan from China shock)
